question.text:
The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y = \dfrac{1}{2}f(x)?$

(Note: Figures not drawn to scale)
question.explanation:
To graph the function $y = \dfrac{1}{2}f(x),$ we take the graph of $y = f(x)$ and compress it by factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y = f(x)$ by $2.$

The resulting graph is the solid blue curve shown below.

example.title: Plotting the Graph of a Vertically Compressed Function

question.text: The point $P$ with coordinates $(4, 0)$ lies on the curve $y =f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y = 4f(x)?$
question.explanation:
The function $y = 4f(x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y = f(x)$ by a factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $4.$

Therefore, the point $(4,0)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $\left(4, 4 \cdot 0\right) = (4, 0),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y = 4f(x).$

example.title: Finding a Point that Lies on a Vertically Scaled Function
